questions.question: What is an irrational number?
options: A real number that is not rational.
A rational number that is not real.
A number that must be an integer.
A number that can always be written as $p/q$ with integers $p,q$ and $q\ \neq 0$.
questions.explanation: By definition, an irrational number is an element of $\mathbb R\setminus\mathbb Q$: real, but not expressible as an integer ratio.

option_explanations: Every rational number is real, so 'rational but not real' describes no number.
Integers are rational because $n=n/1$, so an irrational cannot be required to be an integer.
An expression $p/q$ with integer $q\ne0$ is exactly the definition of a rational number.
